warnings: FACTORIAL DESIGN: Three factors interact - CO2 level (aCO2 vs eCO2), N amendment (with vs without), and fungal species (P. croceum vs T. submollis). Data must be extracted separately for each fungal species and N treatment combination.
FOUR TREATMENT GROUPS per fungal species: aCO2, aCO2+N, eCO2, eCO2+N. The control is aCO2 (no N addition). eCO2 alone vs eCO2+N are both elevated CO2 treatments.
PRIMARY DATA IN FIGURES: Nutrient concentration data (the key outcome for dilution effect) is presented in Figure 1 (bar graphs with means and SD), not in tables - requires reading from figures.

Table 4 contains nutrient CONTENT (total amount per seedling), not nutrient CONCENTRATION. These are different metrics - content includes biomass effect, concentration does not. For dilution effect analysis, concentration data from Figure 1 is more appropriate.

N AMENDMENT CONFOUND: The eCO2+N treatment adds nitrogen fertilizer which could directly increase nutrient concentrations, masking the dilution effect. Extractors should be careful to use eCO2 (without N) vs aCO2 (without N) for clean CO2 effect comparison.

MYCORRHIZAL SPECIES EFFECT IS LARGE: P. croceum and T. submollis produce dramatically different nutrient concentrations (P concentrations >2x higher with P. croceum). Data from the two fungal species should NOT be pooled.
VARIANCE TYPE: Data reported as means ± standard deviation (SD), n=10 rhizotrons. Each rhizotron contained 3 seedlings treated as one entity.
Figure 2 contains nutrient USE EFFICIENCY data (biomass per unit nutrient), NOT nutrient concentrations - do not confuse with primary outcome.
Nutrient concentration data in Figure 1 is split across two panels (Fig. 1 and Fig. 1 continued) for different elements.
The paper reports that treatment effects on nutrient concentrations were mainly significant only in P. croceum seedlings, with T. submollis showing fewer significant treatment effects.

recon.potential_tc_confusion: The aCO2+N treatment adds nitrogen to the ambient CO2 control, which could be mistaken as a treatment. Also, the two fungal species (P. croceum vs T. submollis) create separate sub-experiments that must not be pooled.

recon.extraction_guidance: PRIMARY OUTCOME DATA (nutrient concentrations) is in Figure 1 (bar graphs) - must be read from figures for both fungal species separately. Table 4 contains nutrient CONTENT (total per seedling) which is a secondary metric incorporating biomass. For the dilution effect analysis: (1) Use Figure 1 for concentration data; (2) Extract separately for P. croceum and T. submollis; (3) Use aCO2 (white bars) as control and eCO2 (dark grey bars) as treatment for a clean CO2 comparison without N confound; (4) eCO2+N (black bars) vs aCO2+N (light grey bars) provides a secondary comparison with N amendment. Plant fractions available: shoot (needles+shoot combined), root, and total plant. The paper explicitly states P. croceum nutrient concentrations are significantly higher than T. submollis for most elements, so species must be treated as separate experimental systems. Significant treatment effects on concentrations were mainly found in P. croceum seedlings with reductions under eCO2 and eCO2+N.
